Nitin Nabin accuses Rahul Gandhi of relying on ‘3 crore infiltrators’ instead of voters

Nabin challenges opposition on voter deletion claims

NEW DELHI: BJP national president Nitin Nabin on Sunday accused Congress leader Rahul Gandhi of acting at the behest of foreign powers, alleging that the opposition was attempting to create instability and challenge an elected government under the pretext of defending democracy.Addressing the BJP's 'Loktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hatao' (Save Democracy, Remove Anarchy) march in Haryana ’s Rohtak, Nabin said the party's campaign was aimed at countering what he described as a deliberate attempt to spread chaos across the country.Rashtriya Lok Dal (RLD) president Jayant Chaudhary was also present on the stage.“As we participate in this 'Save Democracy' march, we must address the atmosphere of chaos and instability that is being deliberately spread throughout the nation,” Nabin said.He alleged that Rahul Gandhi was working to further the agendas of foreign powers and seeking to challenge India's democratic system at their direction.“They are the same purveyors of chaos who have recently been sowing discord abroad. Their associates, members of the Communist Party and certain Congress leaders, talk about 'changing the regime.' But this is a government formed by the mandate of the people; no one can even lay a finger on it,” he said.Nabin also questioned the Congress's criticism of electoral outcomes, arguing that the party accepted democratic mandates when it won elections but raised concerns over the electoral process when it lost.“You (Congress) have no faith in the country’s 1.4 billion people. In whom, then, do you place your trust? In 3 crore infiltrators! I ask you, Rahul Gandhi: what exactly is your intention? Why do you challenge democracy?” he said.Citing electoral outcomes in different states, Nabin said the Congress described democracy as having prevailed when it won in Himachal Pradesh and Karnataka, but claimed it was under threat after losing in Haryana, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and West Bengal.He further accused the Congress of seeking to run the country according to the wishes of the Gandhi family, saying that governance should instead be guided by the Constitution.BJP president also targeted the Congress over its allegations of irregularities in electoral rolls and criticism of the Election Commission of India (ECI).Referring to the 1975 Allahabad High Court judgment that set aside then Prime Minister Indira Gandhi's election from Rae Bareli, Nabin accused the Congress of having a history of misusing government machinery during elections.“When Indira Gandhi won an election, the Allahabad High Court ruled that she had won by misusing the entire govt machinery and employing improper means. Her election was completely annulled, and she was barred from contesting elections for six years,” he said.He also challenged Rahul Gandhi's claims regarding the deletion of 13 crore votes, saying the BJP and its National Democratic Alliance (NDA) partners were prepared to provide details of the deletions.“Today, they claim that 13 crore votes have been deleted. I say to you, Rahul Gandhi, that any worker from our party, the NDA, or even one of our local unit presidents can provide a detailed account for every single one of those 13 crore deleted votes,” Nabin said.He added that the BJP was willing to discuss the issue either in public or in Parliament. Nabin also accused the Congress of seeking to protect infiltrators and said BJP and NDA workers would work to ensure their removal from the country.Nabin also criticised the Congress over the 1984 anti-Sikh riots, arguing that the party should have apologised for the violence instead of taking part in protests on the issue of electoral integrity.He referred to former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi's remark after the assassination of Indira Gandhi that “when a big tree falls, the earth shakes”, saying it should have prompted remorse from the Congress leadership.“When our Sikh brethren were being slaughtered, when a full-scale massacre was unfolding, your father remarked that 'when a big tree falls, the earth shakes.' Because of that 'shaking of the earth,' the lives of so many of my Sikh brothers were extinguished. You should have felt remorse for this; you should have apologised,” he said.The BJP president also accused the Congress of practising dynastic politics and alleged that its leaders followed the directions of the Gandhi family rather than democratic principles.His remarks came as the INDIA bloc held its 'Chalo Dilli' march from the Minto Road-Connaught Place junction to Ramlila Maidan in Delhi on Sunday.The opposition alliance is protesting against alleged irregularities in electoral rolls during the Election Commission's Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise and has demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.Congress leader Rahul Gandhi had alleged that shops in Connaught Place were forcibly shut ahead of the march, causing losses to local traders. In a post on X, he said the opposition had encouraged rally participants to shop in the area but found commercial establishments closed.The BJP also organised a separate march in West Delhi to remember the victims of the 1984 anti-Sikh riots, accusing the Congress of holding its political rally on the anniversary of the violence.
Article Summary: BJP leader Nitin Nabin accuses Rahul Gandhi of relying on ‘3 crore infiltrators’ instead of voters. Nabin challenges opposition on voter deletion claims. BJP leader raises 1984 anti-Sikh riots, targets Gandhi family.

NEW DELHI: Former Lok Sabha Speaker Meira Kumar presided over the INDIA bloc's symbolic “public impeachment” of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar on Saturday, seated in a chair steeped in history. The chair was once used by India's first Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru The information was shared by Congress media and publicity department head Pawan Khera, who was involved in organising the event at the residence of Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge at 10, Rajaji Marg in New Delhi.“The chair on which Meira Kumar sat during today's public impeachment proceedings against the CEC was once occupied by the first prime minister of India, Jawaharlal Nehru, the great-grandfather of Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi,” Khera later said in a post on X.“It was Nehru Ji's chair throughout his tenure as prime minister. It witnessed some of the most consequential decisions in our nation's history and carries the weight of that legacy,” he added.Khera said that Meira Kumar, sitting in the same chair, pronounced Gyanesh Kumar “unfit to continue as the Chief Election Commissioner of India”.“Gyanesh Kumar has been rejected by the people of India. It is only a matter of time before he goes,” he said.The INDIA bloc organised the symbolic proceedings, accusing the CEC of allegedly facilitating the deletion of voters' names from electoral rolls and demanding that he be tried in court for treason and jailed.Kumar opened the proceedings, saying the opposition had decided to convene the meeting because of alleged wrongful deletions of eligible voters.“When this issue is raised by the INDIA bloc, there is no accountability. So we have decided that the INDIA bloc will hold a meeting and bring a proposal to remove Gyanesh Kumar,” she said.The resolution was moved by Kharge, seconded by Samajwadi Party leader Harendra Malik and supported by Rahul Gandhi and other opposition MPs and civil society representatives. It was adopted unanimously through a show of hands.Kharge alleged that the right to vote was under threat and accused the Election Commission of functioning at the behest of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and home minister Amit Shah.Rahul Gandhi described the proceedings as a “political weapon” against those who, he alleged, had colluded to destroy people's votes.“I don't think anything like this has ever happened in history,” Gandhi said, adding that “every single institution is closed to us”.“I fully support the motion to impeach Gyanesh Kumar, who should be tried for treason in court and justice should be served,” he said.The BJP criticised the event, accusing the INDIA bloc of making a “mockery” of Parliament and democracy. BJP spokesperson Sambit Patra said the opposition was holding a “mock parliament” and took a swipe at Rahul Gandhi.The symbolic proceedings came ahead of the INDIA bloc's November 1 march and rally at Ramlila Maidan, where opposition leaders are seeking to intensify pressure for the CEC's removal and raise concerns over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
Article Summary: The chair was once used by India's first Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru. Former Lok Sabha Speaker Meira Kumar presided over the symbolic ‘public impeachment’ of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The INDIA bloc accused the CEC of allegedly facilitating the deletion of voters' names from electoral rolls.

Article Title: From Mallikarjun Kharge's lawn, 250 opposition MPs 'impeach' CEC Gyanesh Kumar
Article Text:
INDIA bloc functionaries take part in the proceedings during the ‘public impeachment’ programme against CEC Gyanesh Kumar at the residence of Mallikarjun Kharge in New Delhi Saturday

NEW DELHI: With Rahul Gandhi terming "public impeachment" and Sunday's Ramlila Maidan rally a "dangerous political weapon" targeting Modi-Shah-Gyanesh, the INDIA bloc, in a symbolic move, Saturday passed a "resolution" to "impeach" CEC Gyanesh Kumar accusing it of colluding with the ruling BJP to compromise national election management. It also sought that Kumar be "tried for treason".Six "charges" of "premeditated attack on poll process" - as part of "criminal conspiracy" of BJP, PM Modi and Union minister Amit Shah - span questionable handling of poll rolls, "manipulated" SIR to delete 14 crore voters, illegal changes to Form 6 to block new voters, deletion of voters through software. CEC Kumar has also been accused of ignoring the two ECs in decision making.The "public impeachment" held in the lawns of the residence of Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge involved around 250 MPs from opposition. The venue was designed with Parliament chamber like decor, with former Speaker Meira Kumar in the high chair. LoP Rajya Sabha Kharge tabled the resolution while Rahul concluded the debate, before Meira Kumar put the resolution to vote that was passed by a voice vote. The slogan 'vote chor gaddi chhod' ended the assembly after three hours of debate.Setting the tone, Kharge said Modi has hatched conspiracies to retain power, which include engineering defections, splitting parties, electoral bonds, misuse of agencies, while adding the 2023 "immunity law" for the CEC is another such instrument.Underlining the need for "public impeachment", Kharge said RS and LS rejected the opposition notices for removal of Kumar. Rahul said 15% of 2024 voters have been deleted by SIR, which means the LS polls were illegal. "I can comfortably say Kumar will not survive as CEC. We have enough proof. If BJP keeps him after we reveal what we know, then the BJP game would be clear," he argued.Harendra Malik of SP said SIR has sought to target "PDA voters" of his party ahead of UP polls. Sagarika Ghose of TMC said 2026 Bengal polls were stolen after 29 lakh voters "vanished" under "Vanish Kumar's SIR". John Brittas (CPM), in a searing warning, said India should not be the Germany of 1930s, a parallel also drawn by Mamata TMC's Mahua Moitra.Those who spoke were Mehbooba Mufti (PDP), Arvind Sawant (Shiv Sena), Abhay Sinha (RJD), NK Premachandran (RSP), Sandosh Kumar (CPI), Rajeev Rai (SP), Durai Vaiko (MDMK), Kapil Sibal, Jose Mani (KCM), Devarajan (FB), ET Muhammed Basheer (IUML), Sudama Prasad (CPI-ML), Nasir Aslam (NC), Thol Thirumavalavan (VCK), Baidyanath Ram (JMM). Civil society luminaries like Yogendra Yadav, Nikhil Dey, Sharukh Alam advocate, Anjali Bharadwaj, Noor Shridhar provided incisive arguments and data to put the EC in the dock. Neha Bora of AISA and NSUI volunteer Ritu Barala also spoke.
Article Summary: INDIA bloc passes a "resolution" to "impeach" CEC Gyanesh Kumar. Accuses it of colluding with the ruling BJP to compromise national election management. It also sought that Kumar be "tried for treason"

Ahead of the INDIA bloc's rally at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan on Sunday, the BJP released a poster titled "Thago Ka Mela' (Fair of Thugs)", targeting Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and several other opposition leaders.Designed in the style of a film poster, the graphic, released by BJP Delhi, features Rahul Gandhi, Congress general secretary Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee and Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray, among other INDIA bloc leaders.The poster accuses the opposition leaders of spreading rumours and creating anarchy in the country at the behest of anti-national forces to protect their political interests. Objective - To spread rumors and anarchy in the country at the behest of anti-national forces in order to save their political ground."The poster comes as opposition parties gather at Ramlila Maidan for the INDIA bloc's 'Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao' rally, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the electoral process.Protesters from several states, including Punjab, Rajasthan, Uttarakhand and Himachal Pradesh, reached Delhi to participate in the demonstration. They raised slogans such as "Vote chor, gaddi chhod" and voiced concerns over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and the use of Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs), reported ANI.Some protesters from Punjab alleged that police barricades along the Punjab-Haryana border delayed their journey to Delhi, with several vehicles stranded overnight. Panna Lal Sharma, who travelled from Rajasthan, said he had joined the demonstration to oppose alleged electoral irregularities and demand the use of ballot papers.Uttarakhand Congress secretary Madanpal Singh said the protesters would continue their agitation until the Chief Election Commissioner resigned.The rally mobilisation havre also drawn participants from Himachal Pradesh, some of whom raised concerns over issues such as examination paper leaks, youth-related problems and alleged curbs on democratic rights.According to the rally schedule, INDIA bloc MPs were to assemble at the Constitution Club at 11 am before proceeding towards Ramlila Maidan from the Minto Road-Connaught Place junction at noon.

Article Title: HC nixes NIA plea, upholds bail to J&K terror conspiracy accused
Article Text:
Delhi HC upholds bail granted to alleged J&K terror outfit overground worker, dismisses NIA’s appeal

NEW DELHI: Delhi high court has dismissed NIA's appeal against a trial court order granting bail to an alleged over ground worker in J&K, Mateen Ahmed Bhat, in a terror conspiracy case.A bench of Justices Navin Chawla and Arun Bhardwaj held that the trial court had passed the order after properly considering the restrictions on grant of bail under UAPA and examining whether the accusations against Bhat were prima facie true.The court further said neither was the bail order a final conclusion on the evidence nor did it discharge the accused. The subsequent framing of charges against Bhat was also deemed irrelevant by the bench while deciding NIA's appeal.The case relates to an alleged larger conspiracy involving the activities of proscribed terrorist organisations and the use of online platforms and local operatives to spread unrest in J&K.The high court observed that an appeal against the grant of bail has a limited scope and interference is warranted where the bail order is shown to be illegal, perverse, arbitrary or based on irrelevant considerations.
Article Summary: Delhi HC upholds bail granted to alleged J&K terror outfit overground worker, dismisses NIA’s appeal. NIA's appeal against a trial court order granting bail to Mateen Ahmed Bhat, in a terror conspiracy case.

Article Title: INDIA bloc 'impeaches' CEC in mock Parliament, but what will it take to remove him for real
Article Text:
What will it take to remove CEC Gyanesh Kumar for real

The CEC can be removed by the same procedure as a Supreme Court judge and requires a majority vote from both the Houses.

NEW DELHI: The opposition on Saturday unanimously passed a "resolution" to remove Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over allegations of irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls during a "mock Parliament" organised at Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's residence.Former Lok Sabha Speaker Meira Kumar presided over the proceedings, with several MPs and activists supporting the demand for the CEC's removal.Kharge moved the resolution seeking Kumar's removal, accusing him of centralising control over electoral rolls and acting at the behest of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah. Kharge also said that SIR was initiated to remove voters opposed to Bharatiya Janata Party."The proposal we are bringing today is to safeguard the dignity of a constitutional institution. We have no personal enmity with the CEC. Our intention is that the Election Commission should function impartially in keeping with the spirit of the Constitution," Kharge said."The trust of the common man in it should remain intact. No one sitting in Delhi should be able to wrongly delete the voting rights of weaker sections, women, and youth using a computer," he added.Meanwhile, leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi delivered the closing remarks of the proceedings, describing the event as the opposition's political weapon targeting CEC Gyanesh Kumar, PM Modi and Amit Shah."This looks like a meeting of Lok Sabha MPs, Rajya Sabha MPs, and common citizens. But actually, this is a political weapon," Rahul said.In the "mock Parliament" at Kharge's residence, the opposition sailed through the resolution with a voice vote. But while the numbers may have been on its side there, would the same motion stand a chance in the real Parliament?The removal of a CEC is deliberately difficult.Article 324(5) of the Constitution states that the Chief Election Commissioner can be removed from office only "in like manner and on the like grounds as a judge of the Supreme Court.""The other Election Commissioners shall not be removed from office except on the recommendation of the Chief Election Commissioner," it further says.Article 124(4) of the Constitution, which lays down the procedure for removing a Supreme Court judge, states that a judge can be removed only by an order of the President following an address by each House of Parliament.Such an address must be supported by a majority of the total membership of that House and by a majority of at least two-thirds of members present and voting, in the same session, on the ground of proved misbehaviour or incapacity.The process begins with a notice of motion in either House of Parliament alleging misbehaviour or incapacity. The notice must be signed by at least 100 MPs in the Lok Sabha or 50 MPs in the Rajya Sabha.The presiding officer of the concerned House can admit or refuse the motion after considering the material and information available. If the motion is admitted, an inquiry is conducted into the charges by a committee constituted for the purpose.If the charges are established, the motion must be passed by a majority of the total membership of each House and by a two-thirds majority of members present and voting in both Houses.Once both Houses pass the motion in accordance with these requirements, an address is made to the President, who then issues the order removing the CEC.The President's role at this stage is constitutional and formal once Parliament has passed the required address.Interestingly, this is not the first time when the opposition is gearing up for introducing a resolution seeking CEC's removal.On April 7, Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla and Rajya Sabha Chairperson CP Radhakrishnan had rejected opposition notice, which was signed by 130 Lok Sabha members, 63 Rajya Sabha members, seeking the CEC's removal over alleged partisanship and arbitrariness in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
Article Summary: Opposition passes "resolution" to remove Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. CEC can be removed by the same procedure as a Supreme Court judge and requires a majority vote from both the Houses. Opposition accuses Kumar of centralising control over electoral rolls and acting at the behest of Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

NEW DELHI: Leader of the opposition in Rajya Sabha Mallikarjun Kharge on Saturday accused Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar of facilitating "vote theft" and listed six charges against him at a symbolic "public impeachment" organised by the opposition INDIA bloc.Kharge alleged that the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls was initiated to remove voters opposed to the BJP. The proceedings began at his residence on Rajaji Marg, with former Lok Sabha Speaker Meira Kumar chairing the event.Kharge accused the CEC of centralising control over electoral rolls and acting at the behest of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah.Kharge also accused PM Modi government of using various means to retain power since 2014, including defections, splitting parties, misuse of central agencies and alleged electoral irregularities."The proposal we are bringing today is to safeguard the dignity of a constitutional institution. We have no personal enmity with the CEC. Our intention is that the Election Commission should function impartially in keeping with the spirit of the Constitution. The trust of the common man in it should remain intact. No one sitting in Delhi should be able to wrongly delete the voting rights of weaker sections, women, and youth using a computer," Kharge posted on X.He further alleged that the government had repeatedly tried to retain power through various means."The Modi government has hatched every conspiracy since 2014 to cling to power: stealing MPs, breaking parties, stealing governments, Electoral Bonds, misuse of ED/CBI. And now Vote Theft—cut opposition votes and rule. There are hundreds of examples of Vote Theft," he said.Kharge also criticised the 2023 law governing the appointment of the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC), alleging that it provided the election commissioner with legal protection."Gyanesh Kumar is able to carry out this theft because of the 2023 CEC Act. In December 2023, this bill was passed by suspending 145 opposition MPs. This law gives the CEC a lifelong protective shield that even the President and CJI do not have," he added.Questioning the results of the 2024 Maharashtra and Haryana assembly elections, Kharge alleged that the INDIA bloc's strong performance in the Lok Sabha elections was followed by a reversal in the state polls due to electoral irregularities."In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, we had an excellent performance in Maharashtra and Haryana, but the results flipped in the assembly elections. Reason—votes were illegally added before the elections and then all names were removed. This work is being done together by Modi-Shah and Gyanesh," he alleged.Earlier in the day, Lok Sabha leader of the opposition Rahul Gandhi called on people to join a march in the national capital on Sunday ahead of the INDIA bloc's rally at Ramlila Maidan on November 1.In a post on X, Rahul announced the route and timing of the walk, saying, "See you tomorrow, let's walk together."According to his post, the march will begin at noon from the Minto Road junction near Connaught Place, proceed towards Ajmeri Gate and conclude at Ramlila Maidan.However, Delhi Police sources said no permission had been sought for a march starting from Connaught Place.
Article Summary: Mallikarjun Kharge accused Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar of facilitating "vote theft" He listed six charges against him at a symbolic "public impeachment" organised by the opposition INDIA bloc. Kharge alleged that the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls was initiated to remove voters opposed to the BJP.

NEW DELHI: Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav on Saturday dismissed Union home minister Amit Shah 's claim that the BJP was firmly entrenched in Uttar Pradesh, questioning him over crimes against women and Dalits in the state. Party MP Awadhesh Prasad also hit back at Shah's "Angad's foot" remark, saying the BJP's political footing had "already been uprooted".According to PTI, Akhilesh made the remarks while responding to Shah's assertion that the BJP government in Uttar Pradesh was firmly established and could not be dislodged."Home minister should look into why women face so much injustice in Uttar Pradesh, why the state witnesses so many murders and why people from the Dalit community are among the worst affected," Akhilesh said.He questioned the BJP's claims of political stability in the state, shifting the focus to the government's record on law and order and the treatment of women and Dalits.Reacting to Shah's claim that the BJP government in Uttar Pradesh was firmly entrenched, Samajwadi Party MP Awadhesh Prasad said the party had already lost ground in the state.Responding to Shah's comparison of the BJP's position to "Angad's foot", Awadhesh said, "The foot has already been uprooted."Awadhesh said the BJP had failed to retain several seats in the recent Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council elections despite making every effort. He cited the party's defeats in Varanasi, Lucknow and Agra, and also referred to its loss in Prayagraj, a prominent educational centre.He also pointed to the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, saying the BJP had failed to achieve its target of winning all 80 seats in Uttar Pradesh. The SP won 37 seats, while the Congress secured six, taking the INDIA bloc's tally to 43 seats in the state.Shah made the remarks on Friday while addressing the BJP's state working committee meeting at the Dr Ram Manohar Lohia National Law University auditorium in Lucknow.The meeting was attended by Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, Deputy Chief Ministers Keshav Prasad Maurya and Brajesh Pathak, and other senior BJP leaders. Shah expressed confidence that the BJP would return to power in the 2027 Assembly elections, comparing the party's position in Uttar Pradesh to "Angad's foot" and saying nobody could dislodge it.He also announced that the BJP would implement the Uniform Civil Code (UCC) in Uttar Pradesh if voted back to power. Targeting the Samajwadi Party over the Ram temple issue, Shah referred to the October 30, 1990, police firing on kar sevaks in Ayodhya and accused the SP of ordering firing on Ram devotees, while asserting that the BJP had built the Ram temple.
Article Summary: Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav questions home minister Amit Shah over crimes against women and Dalits in Uttar Pradesh. Party MP Awadhesh Prasad says the BJP's political footing had "already been uprooted" Shah made the remarks on Friday while addressing BJP's state working committee meeting.

'We follow the path shown by Mahatma Gandhi': Dipke

NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke in another X post on Monday claimed that the local Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP) in his hometown had “suddenly gone on leave” and that a new officer had been brought in to take charge.Dipke’s remarks came amid party's earlier claim that he and fellow CJP leaders Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Dass could be arrested before October 10 under the National Security Act (NSA) or other provisions.AISA national president Neha Bora on Monday claimed that protesting journalists have been detained at the Delhi Cantonment Police Station.In a post on X, Neha said "Rosy and other protesting journalists are detained at Delhi Cantt PS. Team of lawyer comrades are in touch with them.But if any lawyer can be at the PS immediately, pls DM."Rosie is among the three female journalists who filed complaint alleging sexual harassment by police personnel during a protest in the New Delhi area on October 3.The complants have been transferred to the Crime Branch at Kamla Market for further action.Delhi Police also detained several protesters outside Parliament Street Police Station who were demonstrating over an alleged incident of sexual misconduct involving three women journalists during an October 3 protest at Jantar Mantar.The protesters alleged that they had been demonstrating since 6pm on Sunday, demanding registration of an FIR in the case. Police detained them around 7am on Monday following a clash, with protesters alleging they were treated poorly despite only seeking registration of an FIR. Trinamool Congress (TMC) MP Derek O’Brien also extended support to Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders as party spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka claimed that multiple sources had warned that the three could be arrested before October 10 under the National Security Act (NSA) or other equivalent provisions.“With you all the way 🪳🪳stay strong. ‘10 Oct poora desh aa raha hai…’,” O’Brien said in a post on X while replying to Dipke.CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke reacting to the claim said they would not be intimidated by the possibility of action under laws such as the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) or National Security Act (NSA).“If the Govt believes that the threat of UAPA, NSA or years behind bars will scare us into silence, it won’t,” Dipke said in a post on X, adding that the protesters were prepared to spend “months or years in jail” but would not back down from their campaign to “save democracy”.He further said that they follow the path shown by Mahatma Gandhi and continue to resist “peacefully and non-violently”, despite what he described as attempts by the state to intimidate them.The developments come amid the CJP-led campaign against the Election Commission’s Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The protesters have been demanding accountability from chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the exercise and have announced further mobilisation on October 10 in Delhi.
Article Summary: AISA national president Neha Bora claims that protesting journalists have been detained at the Delhi Cantonment Police Station. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke reacting to the claim said they would not be intimidated by the possibility of action under laws such as the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act.

Article Title: Punjab polls: In a blow to AAP, 2 MLAs, Chetan Singh Jouramajra and Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra, quit party after 1st candidate list announcement
Article Text:
(R-L) Chetan Singh Jouramajra from Samana and Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra

(With inputs from PTI)





CHANDIGARH: Two AAP MLAs, Chetan Singh Jouramajra from Samana and Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra from Sanour, both in Punjab's Patiala district have resigned from the party's primary membership on Sunday, a day after the Aam Aadmi Party released its first list of 40 candidates for the 2027 assembly elections.The party, however, has not yet announced its candidates for either constituency.According to news agency PTI, Pathanmajra sent his resignation letter to AAP national convener Arvind Kejriwal , Jouramajra, a former Punjab minister, announced his decision in a social media post.The resignations come as AAP begins preparations for the 2027 polls.In September, the party appointed former Punjab minister Surjit Singh Rakhra as its halqa (constituency) in-charge for Samana. Rakhra is being seen as a possible candidate from the seat, although the party has not officially declared him as its nominee.Pathanmajra, meanwhile, has previously questioned the functioning of the AAP government in Punjab.He has also been facing a rape case registered in September last year following a complaint by a woman from Zirakpur. She alleged that Pathanmajra had misrepresented himself as a divorcee, entered into a relationship with her and married her in 2021 despite already being married.The Punjab Police arrested Pathanmajra in Madhya Pradesh's Gwalior in March this year, more than six months after he allegedly escaped police custody in connection with the case.In May, the Punjab and Haryana high court granted him regular bail in the case.
Article Summary: Chetan Singh Jouramajra and Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra resign from the party's primary membership. The resignations come as AAP begins preparations for the 2027 polls. The party, however, has not yet announced its candidates for either constituency.

Article Title: Amit Shah to spearhead BJP’s UP outreach before state polls with 18-rally plan
Article Text:
Union home minister Amit Shah





LUCKNOW: Days after pitching the implementation of the Uniform Civil Code (UCC) as the BJP’s next major agenda item in Uttar Pradesh, Union home minister Amit Shah is set to lead an extensive statewide campaign, with the party planning rallies across all 18 divisions of the state as it begins preparations for the 2027 assembly elections.Party sources said Shah’s address at the BJP state working committee meeting in Lucknow on Friday was the first in a series of proposed engagements aimed at energising the organisation ahead of the electoral battle. He is also likely to be the chief guest at Ayodhya’s Deepotsav celebrations on November 7 and address a public gathering there.After Diwali, Shah is expected to address rallies in the remaining divisions, effectively covering all 18 administrative divisions of Uttar Pradesh.Senior BJP leaders said the exercise is aimed at galvanising booth-level workers and strengthening the party organisation well before the start of the election campaign.The BJP has also proposed at least 20 rallies by Prime Minister Narendra Modi across the state, with a minimum of three programmes in each of the party’s six organisational regions - Kashi, Gorakhpur, Awadh, Kanpur-Bundelkhand, Brij-Rohilkhand and West UP.The final schedule, however, is subject to approval from the Prime Minister’s Office, party leaders said.Addressing over 2,500 party workers at the state working committee meeting, Shah praised the Yogi Adityanath government for the robust law and order and development initiatives, and said a fresh BJP mandate would pave the way for implementation of the UCC in Uttar Pradesh. Drawing parallels with the abrogation of Article 370 and the construction of the Ram temple, he said the BJP had consistently delivered on its ideological commitments.Shah asserted that the BJP’s organisational strength made it a formidable force in the state. He also projected long-term political dominance for the party and urged workers to focus on strengthening the organisation at the grassroots.According to party sources, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath informed the meeting that an invitation had been extended to Shah to attend Deepotsav as chief guest, while BJP national general secretary and UP in-charge Vinod Tawde later told party functionaries that Shah would be addressing rallies across all divisions as part of the organisational mobilisation drive.
Article Summary: Union home minister Amit Shah is set to lead an extensive statewide campaign. The party is planning rallies across all 18 divisions of the state. Shah is also likely to be the chief guest at Ayodhya’s Deepotsav celebrations on November 7 and address a public gathering there.

Article Title: Judge named accused in son’s fatal Mercedes crash gets interim protection from arrest
Article Text:
Jayabalakrishnan, who ran a roadside eatery, was heading home after closing the shop when the accident occurred at 2.20 am on Sunday. Both vehicles were travelling towards Kalamassery.





KOCHI: The Kerala high court on Thursday granted interim protection from arrest to the additional district judge whose 17-year-old son allegedly drove a Mercedes-Benz that hit a two-wheeler in Kochi, killing the rider.Justice Kauser Edappagath passed the order on an anticipatory bail plea filed by the judge, who is posted at a Motor Accident Claims Tribunal in Irinjalakuda, Thrissur district.“The police shall not arrest the applicant until further orders. However, he shall appear before the investigating officer today at 1pm and if necessary as and when called for. The interrogation of the applicant shall be done in accordance with the guidelines laid down by the Supreme Court,” the court ordered.Senior advocate P Vijaya Bhanu, appearing for the judge, told the court that his client had appeared before the police on Wednesday and was interrogated for more than four hours. Another notice directing him to appear before the police had since been issued.According to Bar and Bench, questioning the need for further interrogation and custodial questioning, the court remarked, “What was the need to interrogate him for four hours and now for further interrogation? Why is his arrest required? He is a judicial officer.He will co-operate with the investigation.”Counsel representing the victim’s legal heirs opposed the plea, alleging that the judge had tampered with evidence after being informed of the accident.The court said it had to proceed strictly in accordance with the law and granted interim protection from arrest. It also asked the prosecutor to provide the state’s response to the plea.The judge was named as an accused in the FIR registered after the October 25 crash in Cheranalloor, Kochi, in which his minor son allegedly drove the car that hit a two-wheeler, killing Jayabalakrishnan.In his anticipatory bail plea, the judge claimed he had no knowledge that the vehicle had been taken from the premises. He said he learnt of the accident after receiving a phone call while asleep.The plea also argued that Section 105 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, which deals with culpable homicide not amounting to murder, requires knowledge that the act is likely to cause death.Meanwhile, the victim’s family has complained to the Kerala high court chief justice seeking an inquiry into the judicial officer’s conduct. According to Bar & Bench, the High Court’s Administrative Committee held a preliminary meeting on October 27 and decided to await further material from the investigating agency before taking any action against the judge.
Article Summary: The Kerala high court on Thursday granted interim protection from arrest to the additional district judge. His 17-year-old son allegedly drove a Mercedes-Benz that hit a two-wheeler in Kochi, killing the rider. Justice Kauser Edappagath passed the order on an anticipatory bail plea filed by the judge, who is posted at a Motor Accident Claims Tribunal.

Article Title: NSUI functionaries detained during Jamia protest get bail
Article Text: New Delhi: NSUI functionaries Zeeshan Ahmad and Faizan Ali Khan, who were granted bail on Oct 29, were released Saturday after spending three days in judicial custody at Tihar Jail. They were granted bail on the condition that they “maintain peace” and furnish a surety of Rs 5,000 each.During the protest at Jamia Millia Islamia over its students’ union, Delhi Police had initiated preventive action against them on Oct 28 under sections 126 and 170 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, which deal with preventing breaches of peace and apprehending persons likely to commit cognisable offences. Their release was delayed due to pending formalities, including “surety verification”.Advocate Saimon Farooqui opposed their continued custody for surety verification, arguing that they should be released on “personal bonds” instead.Police alleged that the two were trying to “provoke passersby” and “gather a crowd” outside gate no. 4 of Jamia by raising slogans in support of the students’ union. Their actions, police claimed, could disturb public peace.
Article Summary: NSUI functionaries Zeeshan Ahmad and Faizan Ali Khan, who were granted bail on Oct 29, were released Saturday after spending three days in judicial custody at Tihar Jail. Delhi Police had initiated preventive action against them on Oct 28 under sections 126 and 170 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita.

Article Title: Water in petrol: Sambhajinagar pump owner faces FIR 5 years after complaints
Article Text:
Aurangabad bench of the Bombay high court

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:

TOI





Five years after complaints of petrol mixed with water, Cidco police have registered a case against the owner of a petrol pump on Jalgaon Road in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar.The FIR was registered on the complaint of district supply officer Bharti Wakode under sections 3 and 7 of the Essential Commodities Act. The FIR mentions the findings of the inspection conducted on Nov 16, 2021, the number of customers who had complained at the time, and the laboratory report dated Dec 26, 2022, which confirmed traces of water in petrol.The criminal action follows an order passed by the Bombay high court in a writ petition filed by activist Manish Narwade.“The incident dates back to Nov 16, 2021. On that day, 40 to 50 customers who had filled petrol at the pump complained that water was present in the petrol supplied to them. Following the complaints, an inspection was carried out at the pump and samples were collected,” Narwade said.As per the complaint, samples were drawn from three nozzles at the fuel station and sent to the laboratory for testing. The laboratory report was received on Dec 26, 2022. The report allegedly confirmed the presence of water traces in the samples collected from the three nozzles. However, no offence was registered by authorities, following which Narwade took legal recourse.“Despite the laboratory confirmation in Dec 2022, the FIR was not registered at that time. A writ petition was subsequently filed before the Bombay high court’s Aurangabad bench seeking directions for action based on the inspection and lab report,” Narwade said.Pursuant to the high court order, the district supply office submitted a complaint to Cidco police, based on which the FIR was registered on Oct 23.“The case is significant because it relates to adulteration of fuel with water, which causes damage to vehicles and loss to consumers. The five-year gap between the complaint, the lab report and the registration of the FIR has also brought the issue of delayed action in adulteration cases into focus,” Narwade said.The management of the petrol pump on Jalgaon Road refused to comment when contacted by
Article Summary: Cidco police have registered a case against the owner of a petrol pump on Jalgaon Road in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar. The criminal action follows an order passed by the Bombay high court in a writ petition filed by activist Manish Narwade.

Article Title: Rs 1 lakh bribe trap: Navi Mumbai ACB catches circle officer, talathi and woman assistant
Article Text:
The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite, Jaihind Birsha Koli (49) and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36).





NAVI MUMBAI: The Navi Mumbai Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has arrested two revenue officials and a woman assistant for allegedly accepting a Rs 1 lakh bribe from a villager in Chirner, Uran taluka, to register the names of his relatives in the 7/12 extract of a land record.The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite (52), circle officer at Koproli in Uran taluka; Jaihind Birsha Koli (49), talathi; and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36), an assistant to the revenue officials.Dharmaraj Sonake, deputy superintendent of police, Navi Mumbai ACB, said the complainant had applied to register the names of the heirs of his deceased sister in the 7/12 extract of their land in Chirner.The land was jointly owned by the complainant's maternal uncle, aunt, brother and sister. The complainant had also applied for deletion of his deceased brother's name and submitted the request to circle officer Mohite and talathi Koli. However, the two officials allegedly demanded Rs 1 lakh from him to process the work.Dy SP Sonake said, "After verification of the complaint on Monday, when it was confirmed that the revenue officers Mohite and Koli had told the complainant to hand over the bribe amount to the accused woman assistant Monika Patil, a trap was laid on Tuesday around 2 pm. After the woman assistant Monika Patil accepted the demanded bribe of Rs 1 lakh from the complainant and handed it over to circle officer Keshav Mohite, both were caught red-handed and arrested. While, the acccused Talathi Jaihind Koli who was involved in the bribe demand was taken into custody from Dronagiri."
Article Summary: The Navi Mumbai Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has arrested two revenue officials and a woman assistant for allegedly accepting a Rs 1 lakh bribe. The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite (52), circle officer at Koproli in Uran taluka; Jaihind Birsha Koli (49), talathi; and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36)

Article Title: Man in Mahindra Thar with duplicate plate molests woman, knocks down another in Kharghar
Article Text:
30-year-old man was apprehended for allegedly molesting a woman and injuring another in Navi Mumbai.





NAVI MUMBAI: A 30-year-old man wearing a mask and driving a red Thar SUV with a duplicate registration number plate was apprehended by the Crime Branch Unit-3 team within 10 hours on Thursday evening.He had allegedly molested a 26-year-old woman walking on the street in Kharghar, around 400metres from Pethpada metro station, on September 30 night and, an hour later, severely injured a 22-year-old woman by knocking her down in Belpada, Sector 3, Kharghar.Acting on a complaint by the woman allegedly molested by the Thar SUV driver, Kharghar police registered an FIR under BNS section 74 for the offence of assault or criminal force against a woman with the intent to outrage her modesty.While, as per the complaint by the injured woman Shrawani Dandekar, a resident of sector 3, Belpada, an FIR under relevant BNS sections and Motor Vehicle Act was registered against the Thar SUV driver for rash and negligent driving causing hurt.The detained aaccused identified as Ali alias Talib Ahsan Nakhvi, a resident of sector 50, Seawoods, Nerul was handed over to Kharghar police for further legal action.Previously, in January 2021, he was arrested by Nerul police in the FIR registered against him for alleged kidnapping, sexual harassment and molestation of a woman.Sanjay Joshi, senior inspector of Kharghar said, "The accused Nakhvi has been detained and subsequently it will be decided whether to arrest him or serve with a notice under Bharatiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) for cooperating in police investigating."Audumbar Patil, senior inspector of crime branch unit-3 said, "After an FIR for molestation was registered at Kharghar police station by the victim woman, a resident of sector 34, Kharghar. As per the orders of higher authority, our team started a parallel probe. From the CCTV camera surveillance near the crime scene, we obtained the red Thar SUV's registration number, which was of Vashi RTO passing.""When verified, the registration number was found to be that of a Maruti WagonR car. As the accused had used a duplicate registration number plate, we scrutinized as many as 62 Thar SUVs registered with various Regional Transport Offices (RTOs). Subsequently, we obtained the registration number of a red Thar SUV that was registered with Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar RTO," Patil added.SPI Patil further informed, "The SUV was registered in the name of Ali alias Talib Ahsan Nakhvi, a resident of Devaki Apartment in sector-50, Seawoods. From his mobile number registered with the RTO, his location was tracked.""He was apprehended from Bonkode village, Koparkhairane on Thursday late evening. Upon thorough interrogation, he confessed that he had inappropriately touched the woman pedestrian near Pethpada metro station while he drove his Thar SUV and sped away. He even confessed to have injured a woman pedestrian by hitting her his SUV while driving in Belpada area," he said.
Article Summary: A 30-year-old man wearing a mask and driving a red Thar SUV with a duplicate registration number plate was apprehended by the Crime Branch Unit-3 team on Thursday evening. He had allegedly molested a woman walking on the street in Kharghar, around 400metres from Pethpada metro station, on September 30 night. An hour later, he severely injured a woman by knocking her down in Belpada, Sector 3, KharGHar.

Article Title: 2 women escape from RPF lockup in Navi Mumbai; 1 held after 6 hours, cop suspended
Article Text:
The women removed their sarees, tied one end to the generator on the balcony and climbed down before escaping. (AI image)





NAVI MUMBAI: In a major security lapse at Belapur Railway Protection Force (RPF), two women arrested for allegedly attempting to steal overhead electric wires from the Juinagar railway godown escaped from the lockup after midnight on September 28.One of them was apprehended around six hours later, while the other remains at large.The woman constable on night duty has been suspended and a departmental inquiry has been initiated against her.As per the FIR registered by RPF sub-inspector Milap Parte (52) at Panvel GRP, a case was registered on September 24 under Section 3(a) of the Railway Property (Unauthorized Possession) Act, 1966, Amendment 2012, at Belapur railway police station.The case was based on a written memo submitted by RPF personnel Ravikant Gade regarding the theft of overhead electric wires from the godown at Juinagar railway station on September 21.During the probe, a trap was laid on September 26 and around 1pm, two women were found loitering suspiciously near the Juinagar godown with the alleged intention of committing theft.They were taken into custody and identified as Rupali Kailas Kurhade (30), from Jalna, and Shalibai Ashok Pawar (49), from Bhiwandi.They were arrested after an FIR was registered for attempted theft and produced before a CSMT court, which remanded them to police custody till September 30. They were lodged in the lockup at Belapur RPF police station.Day-shift woman constable Rakhi Malaiya was assigned guard duty at the lockup, after which woman head constable Pooja Bagre was on night duty.Around 2am on September 28, when Bagre had gone to the toilet, the two women allegedly managed to open the lock by inserting their hands through the iron bars of the lockup and jerking it. Police suspect the lock may not have been secured properly.The women then reached the balcony at the rear end of the police station. They removed their sarees, tied one end to the generator on the balcony and climbed down before escaping.The incident was captured on CCTV footage. PSI Parte learnt about the escape after waking up at home around 6.30am and finding several missed calls from head constable Bagre and ASI Rajiv Parsan.Sunil Nila, chief spokesperson of Central Railway, said, "One accused woman Rupali Kurhade was apprehended from near Nerul railway station around 8.45 am. The other accused Shalibai Pawar is still absconding."
Article Summary: The women removed their sarees, tied one end to the generator on the balcony and climbed down before escaping. One of them was apprehended around six hours later, while the other remains at large. The woman constable on night duty has been suspended and a departmental inquiry has been initiated.

Article Title: TMC suspends fire chief over immersion ghats lapses
Article Text:
Thane municipal corporation





THANE: The Thane municipal corporation (TMC) on Friday suspended its acting chief fire officer (CFO) over alleged negligence in providing adequate safety equipment at idol immersion ghats on Oct 20. Action has also been taken against two other officials, while show-cause notices have been served on two junior staff, it is learnt.The suspension order is issued by additional municipal commissioner-1, Prashant Rode, holds Jhalke responsible for lapses in carrying out his duties. The order states that he has been suspended under the Maharashtra Civil Services (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 1979. Jhalke, who is the fire officer and in-charge of Balkum fire station, has been handling the additional charge of CFO for the last several years."Certain safety arrangements at Datta Mandir Ghat and Ahilyadevi Ghat at Masunda Lake were allegedly found to be inadequate, with a particular shortfall in life jackets and other essential safety equipment. The shortcomings were apparently pointed out to deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde who also expressed concern at the alleged negligence," said a civic official.Officials said that during the suspension period, Jhalke will be required to comply with the prescribed conditions and cannot take up other employment or engage in business without the requisite permission.
Article Summary: Thane municipal corporation suspends acting chief fire officer (CFO) over alleged negligence. Action also taken against two other officials, while show- cause notices have been served on two junior staff. Safety arrangements at Datta Mandir Ghat and Ahilyadevi Ghat at Masunda Lake allegedly found to be inadequate.

Article Title: Sealed Thane flat in Iqbal Kaskar-Dawood Ibrahim money laundering case breached; ED reclaims property, files FIR
Article Text:
Thane flat linked to Iqbal Kaskar’s extortion case targeted for occupation





MUMBAI: Enforcement Directorate (ED) filed an FIR for trespassing and attempting to occupy a flat in Thane which was attached in a money laundering case it investigated against Iqbal Kaskar and his Pakistan-based gangster brother Dawood Ibrahim The flat was attached in the case in 2022, in the money laundering case linked to extortion by Iqbal Kaskar and others.The flat was in ED’s possession and it had put its seal on the lock. Kaskar had acquired the flat through extortion and threat in 2015 and got it registered in the name of his associate Mumtaz Azaz Sheikh, alias Raju.Recently, the ED learnt that certain persons entered the flat after removing its possession notice, claiming ownership of the flat.Since the money laundering case is pending in the court, the ED informed the court about it, repossessed the flat and filed a police case last week.
Article Summary: Enforcement Directorate (ED) filed an FIR for trespassing and attempting to occupy a flat in Thane. The flat was attached in a money laundering case it investigated against Iqbal Kaskar and his Pakistan-based gangster brother Dawood Ibrahim. The ED repossessed the flat and filed a police case last week.

Article Title: Will move court if Chandiwal panel report not made public: Deshmukh
Article Text:
Nagpur:





Former Maharashtra home minister Anil Deshmukh has urged the governor to intervene and ensure the public release of the Justice Chandiwal Commission report on the Rs100 crore extortion allegations against him. Deshmukh warned of approaching the court if the state govt failed to disclose its findings.Deshmukh said the commission, headed by retired Justice Chandiwal, conducted a 13-month inquiry and submitted its nearly 1,400-page report to the state govt around four years ago. Chief minister Devendra Fadnavis hasn’t responded to around 15 letters sent by him, Deshmukh claimed.“I have no objection if the report establishes the allegations against me. Let me face the consequences. But if the allegations have not been proved, that too should be made public,” Deshmukh said, demanding that the report be released during the upcoming legislative session.On preparations for the Nashik Kumbh Mela, Deshmukh alleged irregularities in projects involving expenditure of Rs35,000 crore to Rs40,000 crore and sought an inquiry into complaints by locals over the quality of work and alleged corruption.He also accused the BJP and Shiv Sena of lacking coordination despite sharing power in Maharashtra, claiming that mutual distrust between the allies had affected their electoral performance.Referring to the Nagpur graduates’ constituency election, Deshmukh said votes secured by Nitesh Karale reflected support for Maha Vikas Aghadi’s ideology, while second-preference votes helped Abhijeet Wanjarri emerge victorious.Deshmukh further alleged growing public resentment against the BJP, citing social media criticism of its leaders. He also urged the state govt to prioritise drought relief and assistance to distressed farmers over expensive infrastructure projects, including the proposed Shaktipeeth expressway.
Article Summary: Former Maharashtra home minister Anil Deshmukh has urged the governor to intervene and ensure the public release of the Justice Chandiwal Commission report on the Rs100 crore extortion allegations against him. He warned of approaching the court if the state govt failed to disclose its findings. Chief minister Devendra Fadnavis hasn’t responded to around 15 letters sent by him.

Article Title: Runaway schoolgirls from Vellore rescued in Chennai
Article Text:
Chennai:





Two schoolgirls, aged 16 years, who left their homes in Pernampattu in Vellore district on Friday, were found near a hospital on New Avadi Road in Kilpauk on Saturday morning.A head constable from the Chennai corporation vigilance department spotted them and handed them over to the Kilpauk police.The girls, Pooja and Livasri, studied Class XI at a govt girls’ higher secondary school in Pernampattu. They left their homes on Oct 30 morning, but did not reach the school.Police said the girls travelled to Gudiyatham to meet a friend. After the school informed their parents about their absence, the parents called and reprimanded them. The girls then travelled from Gudiyatham to Bengaluru by train and later reached Chennai Central railway station around 4.30am on Saturday.They took a bus from the railway station and got down on New Avadi Road, where head constable Vasanthakumar spotted them near Murugan Hospital around 8.30am. He took them to G3 Kilpauk police station. After an inquiry, the Kilpauk police transferred the girls to K6 T P Chathiram police station, which was coordinating with Pernampattu police. Their parents have been informed.
Article Summary: The girls, Pooja and Livasri, studied Class XI at a govt girls’ higher secondary school in Pernampattu. They left their homes on Oct 30 morning, but did not reach the school. A head constable from the Chennai corporation vigilance department spotted them and handed them over to the Kilpauk police.

Article Title: Plea in Madras high court against extension of special officers tenure for rural local bodies
Article Text:
Chennai:





A lawyer has moved the Madras high court , challenging the Tamil Nadu govt’s decision to extend the tenure of special officers appointed to administer rural local bodies in nine districts. He alleged that the move violates the constitutional requirement to conduct local body elections within the prescribed five-year term.The plea moved by advocate R Baskaran is likely to be taken up for hearing in the first week of Nov. The petitioner also urged the court to direct the authorities to complete ward delimitation and reservation procedures within a stipulated timeframe and conduct elections to rural local bodies across 37 districts in the state.According to the petitioner, the elected representatives of village panchayats, panchayat unions, and district panchayats in 28 districts completed their five-year tenure on Jan 5, 2025. The govt then appointed officials from the rural development and panchayat raj department as special officers to administer these local bodies. Their tenure was extended every six months.The govt has now extended the tenure of special officers in these 28 districts until April 19, 2027.Similarly, the tenure of elected representatives in nine other districts — Kancheepuram, Chengalpattu, Villupuram, Kallakurichi, Vellore, Ranipet, Tirupattur, Tirunelveli and Tenkasi — ended on Oct 19. The govt appointed special officers to administer these rural local bodies for another six months, until April 19, 2027, he said.“The govt had cited the merger of 46 rural local bodies with urban local bodies, the creation of nine new panchayat unions and 93 new village panchayats, and the need for ward delimitation and reservation in 23 districts as reasons for its inability to conduct elections,” he added.However, the govt order did not specify any reasons necessitating the promulgation of an ordinance. He also alleged that the state election commission was not consulted before appointing special officers to administer the rural local bodies, he said.Citing Supreme Court judgments, the petitioner argued that ward delimitation could not be cited as a reason for postponing local body elections.
Article Summary: A lawyer has moved the Madras high court challenging the Tamil Nadu govt’s decision to extend the tenure of special officers appointed to administer rural local bodies in nine districts. The plea moved by advocate R Baskaran is likely to be taken up for hearing in the first week of Nov.

Article Title: Former AIADMK MLA, others booked for insulting and intimidating petrol bunk employees near Dharmapuri
Article Text: DHARMAPURI: A case has been registered under the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act against A Govindasamy, former Pappireddipatti AIADMK MLA, and others on charges of humiliating and intimidating petrol bunk employees near Dharmapuri.The complainant is R Arunkumar, 37, of Vellalapatti, who has been working at CKM Bharat Petrol Bunk in Rajapettai for the past six months. In his complaint, Arunkumar stated that Govindasamy and his accomplices, numbering more than 30, arrived at the petrol bunk around 10.45am on Oct 26.Arunkumar alleged that the former MLA obstructed vehicles entering the bunk for refuelling and verbally abused him using obscene language and caste-based slurs. Arunkumar stated that his coworker, Nandakumar, who questioned the behaviour, was also assaulted by those who accompanied the former MLA.Arunkumar approached the Dharmapuri superintendent of police A K Arun Kabilan on Friday seeking action against Govindasamy and others under the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act.Following an inquiry led by Dharmapuri deputy superintendent of Police Sivaraman, a case was registered against the former MLA and others at the Dharmapuri Town B-1 police station.
Article Summary: A case has been registered under the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act. The complainant is R Arunkumar, 37, of Vellalapatti, who has been working at CKM Bharat Petrol Bunk in Rajapettai for the past six months.

Article Title: 864 bottles of liquor seized from house near Erode; man arrested
Article Text: ERODE: Police seized 864 bottles of Indian made foreign liquor (IMFL) from a house near Mylambadi in Erode district in the early hours of Thursday and arrested a man.Acting on a tip-off that bottles of liquor had been illegally stored for unauthorised sale, the Bhavani police conducted a raid at the house of K Govindaraj, 28, of Ammapalayam. They found 864 bottles of IMFL stocked in the house for illegal sale.Police registered a case and arrested Govindaraj. He was remanded in judicial custody.They launched a search for Sekar alias Ammasai, 34, and Sridhar, 38, who have links with the illegal liquor operation.
Article Summary: Police seized 864 bottles of Indian made foreign liquor (IMFL) from a house near Mylambadi in Erode district. Acting on a tip-off that bottles of liquor had been illegally stored for unauthorised sale, the Bhavani police conducted a raid.

Article Title: Stalin gives zero marks to TVK govt, EPS gives “less than zero”
Article Text:
DMK president M K Stalin





Madurai/Trichy: DMK president M K Stalin on Friday gave chief minister C Joseph Vijay’s five-month-old govt zero marks, while AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K Palaniswami said he would give less than zero marks.Speaking to reporters after paying homage to Muthuramalinga Thevar at Pasumpon in Ramanathapuram district, Stalin alleged that rising crime, skyrocketing prices and political vendetta against opposition leaders were the achievements of the govt.On police cases against former DMK ministers, he said, “We will face it legally. We will prove in court that we are not offenders.” Stalin said DMK would not be deterred by such cases as the party has faced Emergency as well as tough laws like MISA, TADA and POTA.Stalin said disillusionment with the administration had spread even among TVK voters, accusing Vijay of treating CM’s post like a nine-to-five job.He cited sexual assaults, missing girls and the escape of 17 inmates from Theni sub-jail as examples of an alleged breakdown in law and order.Earlier in the day he posted a video message on X, Stalin said Vijay should discharge duties of the chief minister before trying to play the role of “thaai maaman” or “annan.” He alleged that TVK administration neither has administrative efficiency on its own nor the sense to listen and act on advice given by others. He said Saturday’s DMK women’s wing demonstrations across district headquarters would be a “wake-up call” for the govt.Speaking to reporters at Trichy airport, EPS said that law and order in Tamil Nadu has plunged to abysmal levels. “People have doubts whether they will be able to return home safely everyday. I will give only ‘minus zero’ marks to the TVK govt’s performance,” he said.On AIADMK’s stand in the five assembly by-elections, he said, “The decision will be taken after the election is announced.”When reporters asked whether those who were expelled from the AIADMK would be taken back into the party, EPS, “Those who were expelled would remain expelled.”
Article Summary: DMK president M K Stalin on Friday gave chief minister C Joseph Vijay’s five- month-old govt zero marks. Stalin alleged that rising crime, skyrocketing prices and political vendetta against opposition leaders were the achievements of the govt.

Article Title: Seeman open to DMK-AIADMK support in Ambasamudram bypoll
Article Text:
Seeman open to DMK-AIADMK support in Ambasamudram bypoll

Madurai:





NTK chief Seeman on Friday expressed willingness to accept support from arch-rivals DMK and AIADMK in the Ambasamudram bypoll, raising the prospect of opposition parties uniting against the ruling TVK.Speaking after paying homage to Muthuramalinga Thevar at Pasumpon, Seeman used a biryani analogy when asked whether he would accept their backing. “If a hungry man is offered biryani, would he refuse it? We will accept it,” he said.Seeman maintained that electoral support should not be mistaken for an alliance. “Political criticism is one thing; ideological positions are another,” he said, referring to his attacks on Stalin and AIADMK head Edappadi K Palaniswami . He clarified that neither party had decided to field him as a common candidate and accused TVK functionaries of fuelling the speculation.Seeman, who announced his candidature on Thursday, urged voters to give him an opportunity to demonstrate his performance in the assembly. Promising to transform Ambasamudram into a model constituency, he challenged Vijay’s TVK to a direct contest with NTK to establish their respective political strength.His remarks gained significance after DMK president M K Stalin , questioned at Pasumpon about supporting Seeman, stopped short of ruling out the possibility.“Let the election date be announced first. We will decide on that afterwards,” Stalin said.The vacancy arose after AIADMK legislator Esakki Subaya, who won the 2026 assembly election by 10,245 votes over Congress candidate VP Durai, resigned and joined TVK. TVK’s S Rajagopal finished third with 53,611 votes, while NTK’s V Sivasankaran secured 14,906 votes.
Article Summary: NTK chief Seeman open to DMK-AIADMK support in Ambasamudram bypoll. Seeman used a biryani analogy when asked whether he would accept their backing. DMK president M K Stalin stopped short of ruling out the possibility.

Article Title: Murder suspect arrested near Krishnagiri
Article Text: KRISHNAGIRI: The Krishnagiri district police on Saturday arrested a man on charges of murdering a 70- year-old woman in Pannandur village.District superintendent of police GS Anitha said, Chamundeeswari, who was living alone, was found dead under suspicious circumstances in her house on Friday morning.During investigations, police found that Suryakumar alias Surya,30, of the same village entered Chamundeeswari’s house around 1am on Friday with an intention to steal valuables. “Acting on the findings, special police teams launched a search operation and arrested the man within 12 hours of the crime,” the SP said.
Article Summary: Chamundeeswari, who was living alone, was found dead under suspicious circumstances in her house on Friday morning. Police found that Suryakumar alias Surya,30, of the same village entered the house with an intention to steal valuables.

Article Title: PE teacher suspended after national flag turns upside down at state sports meet in Salem
Article Text: SALEM: A physical education teacher has been suspended following a protocol lapse during the opening ceremony of the state-level 67th Republic Day Athletics Competitions held at the Mahatma Gandhi Sports Ground here on Wednesday.The incident occurred when the state transport minister A Vijay Tamilan Parthiban was hoisting the national flag, and a snag in the rope caused the flag to fly upside down. The event was organized by the state school education department.Taking immediate note of the negligence during the flag-hoisting ceremony, Salem chief educational officer A Ellappan issued an order placing physical education teacher John Jamindar who had supervised the flag hoisting area.
Article Summary: A physical education teacher has been suspended following a protocol lapse during the opening ceremony of the state-level 67th Republic Day Athletics Competitions. The incident occurred when the state transport minister A Vijay Tamilan Parthiban was hoisting the national flag. A snag in the rope caused the flag to fly upside down.

Article Title: Two history-sheeters who escaped from Attayampatti police station nabbed
Article Text: SALEM: Two history-sheeters, who escaped from the Attayampatti police station in Salem district on Tuesday, were nabbed in the early hours of Wednesday.The duo, identified as Santhosh Kumar and Prabhu, are residents of Kandarkula Manickam near Attayampatti. According to police, Santhosh Kumar and Prabhu were brought to the Attayampatti police station on Tuesday morning in connection with robbery and theft cases and questioned by sub-inspector Krishnan and other police personnel. Subsequently, cases were registered against them.Later, police were making arrangements to produce them before a court in the evening. “However, taking advantage of an opportunity, Santhosh Kumar and Prabhu managed to escape from the police station,” said a police officer.Special police teams were formed to trace them. After an intensive search operation, the duo were tracked down and arrested from near Tiruchengode around 3am on Wednesday.They were brought back to the Attayampatti police station for further inquiry. Later, they were lodged in the Salem Central Prison under judicial custody.
Article Summary: The duo, identified as Santhosh Kumar and Prabhu, are residents of Kandarkula Manickam near Attayampatti. They were brought to the police station on Tuesday morning in connection with robbery and theft cases and questioned by sub- inspector Krishnan and other police personnel.
